purpose: Forecast future unseen malicious transitions using a model trained only on benign network dynamics, not attack-family classification.
source: Official CTU IoT-23 timestamped Zeek conn.log.labeled scenarios
development_selection_note: These are the already-frozen V23 clean-onset development families. V24 results were development evidence; V26 changes the model family but does not unlock or score any final-validation family.
final_validation: remains locked; no final family is scored in V26

temporal_protocol.positive: complete benign 8-minute history ending 30-240 seconds before held-out-family onset
temporal_protocol.negative: complete benign history followed by a complete benign 4-minute future
temporal_protocol.block_split: deterministic one-hour block split inherited from V23; held-out-family-exposed blocks are excluded from train/calibration/policy
temporal_protocol.threshold: fixed 1% policy-benign quantile; no attack-labelled policy example and no test score selects the threshold

feature_policy.state: V23 global network state: flow/topology/concentration, byte/packet/duration, protocol/service/state occupancy and hashed destination-port occupancy
feature_policy.causal_normalization: each cutoff uses only its preceding 8-minute history median and IQR

model.family: benign-only second-order multi-output Ridge network dynamics
model.training_examples: only train-split sequences whose full history and next four minutes are benign

claim_boundary: A pass supports future warning on these development attack behaviours while the model itself is fit only to benign dynamics. It does not prove detection of every zero-day attack.
